newsitem.title: USA: U.S. Diagnostic named in shareholder suit.
newsitem.headline: U.S. Diagnostic named in shareholder suit.

text.p: U.S. Diagnostic Inc was named in a shareholder class action lawsuit that accuses the company of failing to disclose that one of its founders had pleaded guilty to fraud, attorneys for the plaintiffs said in separate statements.
The company was not immediately available for comment.

U.S. Diagnostic, however, had said on December 23, 1996 that Keith Greenberg, the person in question, has worked as a consultant for the company and was not a co-founder. Also, Greenberg has never served as an officer or director.
U.S. Diagnostic had said that its public filings are "correct in all material aspects."

The lawsuit was filed in U.S. District Court for the Southern District of Florida on behalf of all purchasers of U.S. Diagnostic Inc common stock between March 15, 1996 and December 23, 1996, the law firms said.
The law firms claimed that Greenberg's background was never disclosed in Securities and Exchange Commission filings.
The law firms involved include Wolf Popper LLP; Burt & Pucillo; Starr & Holman LLP; and Milberg, Weiss, Bershad, Hynes & Lerach LLP, the companies said in separate statements.
